input.question: Why do scars heal but leave a mark?
input.ground_truth: The skin you were born with took months to carefully grow in a controlled environment. When it gets badly damaged, your body doesn't have the time or conditions to replace it with identical tissue, so it rushes out a job to seal the wound, leaving out stuff like hair follicles and sweat glands to get the job done quicker.

Question: Why do scars heal but leave a mark?

Okay! Imagine your skin is like a piece of paper. When you get a cut, it's like the paper gets torn. When your body fixes the tear, it uses something like tape (but it's not real tape—it's your body's way of healing). The tape is a little different from the paper, so when the cut is all healed up, you can still see a line where the tear was. That line is called a scar.

So, your body fixes the cut (that’s healing), but the way it fixes it leaves a little mark behind (that’s the scar). That’s why scars stay!
